title: Implementation and Evaluation of “ACT PROTECT – Acceptance and Commitment Training for Prevention, Resilience and Occupational Team Engagement in Clinical Hygiene”.
summary:
Healthcare employees often face considerable demands in their daily work. Time pressure, high levels of responsibility, and difficult decisions can lead to stress, exhaustion, and reduced well-being over time. This also applies to employees working in hospital hygiene and central laboratory services.

This study examines a training program specifically developed for these occupational groups. The program aims to help participants cope better with work-related stress, difficult thoughts, and unpleasant emotions. It also aims to support them in building on their personal strengths and acting in accordance with their own values and goals, even in challenging situations.

The study aims to find out how well the program can be implemented in everyday working conditions, how it is received by participants, and whether it can improve their well-being and ability to cope with stress.

Employees from the hospital hygiene departments and the central laboratory of the University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein will take part in the study. The program consists of seven weekly group sessions, each lasting 90 minutes. Three groups will start the training at different times. This allows changes during the training to be compared with changes during the waiting periods.

Participants will complete questionnaires about their well-being and how they deal with work-related and personal challenges before, during, and after the training, as well as several weeks later. This will help determine whether the training is beneficial and whether any improvements are maintained over time.
conditions: Psychological distress among healthcare employees working in hospital hygiene and central laboratory services.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Sufficient proficiency in the German language.
- Employment in the Hospital Hygiene Department or the Central Laboratory of the University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH) at the Kiel or Lübeck campuses.
Exclusion criteria:
Anticipated inability to participate regularly and fully in the offered prevention program.
